claims.title: Capture a matched photon at finite time and compose a relative phase without inventing an inverse

quoted_fields.interface: Declared one-excitation capture/hold/release, h=I+A on the half line, matched external photon preparation, root coupling off while capturing, calibrated disconnected pi/U hold and common root-blind release. For workspace composition require word-preserving fresh flags, actual adjoint decoding and declared conserved charge. TLS stability requires compression of a positive one-body form.
quoted_fields.failure: Special photon and exact/finite timing/control access are supplied and paid. Common release preserves relative phase error but need not restore an original waveform. Hopping-only inverse is a rotating-frame identity unless known onsite phase is tracked/compensated, and cannot reverse an uncontrolled radiation bath. Stable all-number-sector energy is not unrestricted capacity or multiphoton gate dynamics.

claims.title: Trade transfer time against exposure while keeping Markov loss separate from coherent radiation

quoted_fields.interface: One-excitation normalized trajectory with supplied complete Hamiltonian, total coupling bound and diagonal endpoint block where no bypass is required. Markov conclusions need the declared positive loss operator/dilation. Continuum no-go requires stationary W(omega)=v(omega)R on an open interval, finite-duration sources and initially empty radiation.
quoted_fields.failure: An ideal Markov dose is not an exact floor for arbitrary closed radiation. Occupation alone gives no uniform finite-band radiation floor without temporal/control resources. A nontrivial collective kernel alone does not supply controllability; independent channels can remove it. Dipole formulas are free-space point-dipole Born–Markov/RWA estimates with paid exchange, not a universal device constraint.

Passive reciprocal no-go applies to stationaryH/real endpoints with continuous spectral weight, with dark/chiral/time-dependent/approximate exceptions.
